definitions.explanation: The rate at which something moves or happens. Used for physical speed (of vehicles, movement) and figurative speed (of work, progress).

examples.japanese: スピードを{出|だ}しすぎないで。
この{道路|どうろ}はスピード{制限|せいげん}が{時速|じそく}50キロだ。
examples.english: The speed limit on this road is 50 km/h.

examples.japanese: もう{少|すこ}し{仕事|しごと}のスピードを{上|あ}げないと{締|し}め{切|き}りに{間|ま}に{合|あ}わない。
examples.english: If I don't pick up the pace at work a bit more, I won't make the deadline.

notes:
USAGE:
スピード is the standard loanword for speed and is used more frequently than the native {速度|そくど} in everyday conversation, though {速度|そくど} is preferred in technical and formal contexts.

スピード{違反|いはん} (speeding violation) and スピード{制限|せいげん} (speed limit) are common in traffic-related contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- スピードを{出|だ}す: to speed up, to go fast
- スピードを{落|お}とす: to slow down
- スピード{制限|せいげん}: speed limit
- スピード{違反|いはん}: speeding violation
- スピードアップ: speedup, acceleration
